data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Ushma’ meaning ‘rain’ and ‘Ishana’ meaning ‘lord’. Umesh represents the god of rain and is often associated with the monsoon season and new beginnings. The name Umesh carries the meaning “God of Rain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Umesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of rain and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: Umesh carries a profound spiritual meaning, symbolizing the all-powerful lord of rain and the benefactor of nature. As a name, Umesh also serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things and the role that the divine plays in sustaining and nurturing life.

vedic_reference.note: Umesh is a common name in Hinduism and is derived from the name of the goddess Uma, who is often depicted as the dark night sky, and the prefix Ish, which means conquered. Umesh is thus a symbolic name for the one who has conquered the darkness.
